prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Liberal Democrats present the real alternative, built on Freedom, Fairness and Trust, with a green thread through every policy and an internationalist outlook. We opposed the Iraq war and ID cards, reject centralised targets and unfair taxes, and will restore honesty, local power and civil liberties.

How we’ll pay for it
- Switch around £5bn a year from low-priority spend (abolish costly DTI subsidies; scrap ID cards; redirect the Child Trust Fund) and make taxes fairer.
- One net tax rise: a 50% rate on income above £100,000 to fund three fair priorities: abolish tuition/top‑up fees, free personal care, and lower local taxes by replacing Council Tax with a Local Income Tax (typical household saves ~£450 a year).

NHS and care
- Free personal care for older and disabled people.
- More staff (8,000 doctors, 12,000 nurses, 18,000 therapists), cut red tape and Whitehall targets; decisions by clinicians and locally elected bodies.
- Faster diagnosis via more scans/tests (including evenings/weekends), publish waits; free eye/dental checks; fairer prescription exemptions; stronger mental health rights; prevention first (school meal standards, ban smoking in enclosed public places).

Education and skills
- Scrap tuition/top‑up fees and restore fair grants; universities properly funded.
- Cut infant/junior class sizes by hiring 21,000 teachers using Child Trust Fund money; extend wraparound care and Children’s Centres.
- Subject-qualified teaching in core areas; fewer high‑stakes tests; robust discipline; stronger special needs support; a 14–19 diploma blending academic/vocational routes; invest in world‑class colleges; protect free school transport rights.

Crime and liberty
- 10,000 extra police funded by dropping ID cards; cut police paperwork with better tech.
- Target traffickers and acquisitive crime, not personal cannabis possession.
- Tough community penalties that repay victims; rehabilitation that reduces reoffending.
- Defend due process: protect jury trial, repeal flawed control orders, admit intercept evidence; create a UK Border Force; fair, faster asylum with right to work; Single Equality Act and hate‑crime units.

Economy and business
- Maintain stability (NAO scrutiny of budgets); simpler, fairer taxes.
- Replace Council Tax with Local Income Tax; raise stamp duty threshold to £150,000.
- Back an open, reforming EU; prepare for euro entry via tests and referendum.
- Small‑business rate relief; “sunset” unnecessary regulations; single inspections; abolish the DTI and reinvest in skills; legal duty to trade fairly; boost tourism.
- Green economics: shift the Climate Change Levy to a Carbon Tax; incentives for clean cars/homes; at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; no new nuclear; develop hydrogen.

Homes, pensions and welfare
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; shift VAT to favour brownfield reuse; manage second homes in hotspots.
- Citizen’s Pension based on residency; +£100/month at 75 with an earnings link; Local Income Tax helps 8 in 10 pensioners.
- Scrap the CSA (move to Inland Revenue with fair appeals); reform the New Deal; extend Winter Fuel Payment to severely disabled people and allow insulation vouchers; protect workers in failed pension schemes.

Transport and environment
- Fix rail with longer, fewer franchises; redirect some roads spend to rail safety and upgrades.
- Encourage congestion charging with upfront transit investment; reform VED to reward low‑emission cars and move toward national road pricing; free off‑peak buses for pensioners/disabled; restrain major road‑building; per‑aircraft, not per‑passenger, aviation charges; oppose SE airport expansion.
- Lead on climate change (meet Kyoto early; pursue “contraction and convergence”); zero‑waste goal; tougher enforcement on polluters.

Europe, world and defence
- Support an effective, democratic EU and its constitution via referendum; increase aid to 0.7% of GNI by 2011; fair trade and debt relief; ethical arms controls.
- Iraq: illegal war must never recur; support a UN‑led transition and aim to withdraw UK forces with the UN mandate.
- Support our forces, reform procurement, share burdens through NATO/EU; retain a minimum deterrent while pursuing global disarmament.

Clean, accountable government
- Curb prime‑ministerial power with a War Powers Act and a Civil Service Act; stronger select committees.
- Fair votes (STV) for all elections; votes at 16; predominantly elected second chamber; devolve power and cut quangos; make the BBC’s regulator independent of government.
